pr_title: Fix ZipArchiveEntry names shown as corrupted on other zip programs
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65750
Due to changes in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/59442, _generalPurposeBitFlag didn't have the proper value when it was written here:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/afc2f118e7177107655c5f7bf5d02df9953a2742/src/libraries/System.IO.Compression/src/System/IO/Compression/ZipArchiveEntry.cs#L874

A test may or may not be required as .NET is resilient to the error reported, I think is because it decodes with UTF8 regardless. cc @GrabYourPitchforks.

issue_context.title: ZipArchive corrupts files with unicode characters
issue_context.body:
### Description

Discovered this as part of a SDK upgrade in the dotnet/aspnetcore repo. AspNetCore has test assets with unicode chars that get bundled up by Helix:

* https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/tree/main/src/Middleware/StaticFiles/test/UnitTests/SubFolder/%E4%BD%A0%E5%A5%BD/%E4%B8%96%E7%95%8C
* https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/blob/dd1e882f0945121bd0786b4894073db2bd45274c/src/Microsoft.DotNet.Helix/JobSender/Payloads/DirectoryPayload.cs#L53-L68

Updating to the latest SDK causes the folder to be corrupted and our tests to fail:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/174281/155240904-bd0d46bb-0644-4cff-8c12-aabf779eb277.png)


### Reproduction Steps

Run this app using the latest runtime: https://github.com/pranavkm/zip-file

### Expected behavior

Archive should preserve unicode characters 

### Actual behavior

They are garbled

### Regression?

Regression from 7.0-preview2 runtime

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

_No response_

### Other information

_No response_
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).
@carlossanlop perhaps this is related to your recent change: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/59442/files

The entry name encoding may be changed if the comment encoding changes, and viceversa. Per the zip spec, this is the expected behavior, but the change I introduced could've also introduced a bug.

Do you know if the entry was added with a comment?

> Do you know if the entry was added with a comment?

The Helix SDK uses `ZipArchive.ZipArchive(...)` w/ a `MemoryStream` and adds files using `ZipArchive.CreateEntryFromFile(...)`. See https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/blob/main/src/Microsoft.DotNet.Helix/JobSender/Payloads/DirectoryPayload.cs
Ping @carlossanlop have you had a chance to look at this as yet? If not, are you open to rolling back your earlier change since it blocks SDK ingestion in to AspNetCore?

Re-opening the issue per discussion in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/40353#issuecomment-1064369745.

cc/ @carlossanlop, @Jozkee
@TanayParikh @wtgodbe were your issues related to our zip changes after all? do they need to be addressed by the libraries team?
We're all good, we just needed an SDK update to get things aligned.

review_comments: This is fine, since you're avoiding removing the bit flag unexpectedly if filename already set it to true.
I am not sure if I understand. When Utf8 is detected, we enable the Unicode flag?

Yes. Maybe the name of the flag should be `utf8FileNameAndComment` to be very clear.

Per the spec: https://pkware.cachefly.net/webdocs/casestudies/APPNOTE.TXT

```
 Bit 11: Language encoding flag (EFS).  If this bit is set,
                the filename and comment fields for this file
                MUST be encoded using UTF-8. (see APPENDIX D)
```

> Yes. Maybe the name of the flag should be utf8FileNameAndComment to be very clear.

That would definitely help ;) thanks for the pointer to the docs!
I'm ok with removing this if we are directly modifying the general purpose bit flag when detecting the comment or filename encoding.

The problem is that if the comment has utf8 characters, but the filename does not, now you're removing the utf8 flag.

My intention was to detect utf8 characters in either filename or comment. If one of the two had them, then the general purpose bit flag bit 11 would be turned on. Hence the `|=`.
This should probably look like the code you added in the `Comment` setter.

Keep in mind that the `FullName` setter is private, because the name is only set _once_, in the constructor. The user cannot change it. They have to create a new `ZipArchiveEntry` instance if they want to change the name.
Hmm now that I think of it more, maybe it makes sense to set it to 0 or 1 here, since as I said, this is called in the constructor only, which means Comment has not modified this bit yet.
adding/removing the flag was being performed before your changes so this is really going back to update _generalPurposeBitFlag in the ctor before it spreads.
